body:
## Bug Description

External memory providers were silently dropped from session prefetch whenever a healthy recall took longer than 8 s. The prefetch thread join uses the hardcoded `_EXTERNAL_PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S = 8.0`; a still-running provider is then skipped ("Memory provider '…' prefetch timed out after 8.0s; skipping it until the stuck call returns") and the session starts without its long-term memory context. A production audit against a self-hosted memory API recorded 18–27 s recalls and ~53 dropped prefetches in one day; after a reranker-side mitigation, recalls measure 4.39–6.24 s (n=10), with the worst sample still at 78 % of the 8 s bound.

## Root Cause

The external-provider prefetch bound was tuned below real external recall latency. Unlike the stuck-provider case it was written for, a slow-but-healthy call is not distinguishable at the join: both are dropped at the bound.

## Fix

- Raise `_EXTERNAL_PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S` from `8.0` to `12.0` (~2× the measured worst case), keeping a wedged provider bounded.
- Record the measurement basis in the comment next to the constant.

## How to Verify

1. On the base commit, run `pytest tests/agent/test_memory_provider.py::TestMemoryManager::test_default_external_prefetch_timeout_keeps_slow_but_real_recalls` — it fails with the production symptom (`prefetch timed out after 8.0s; skipping it` and empty merged context).
2. Apply the change and re-run — the slow provider's context is kept (`9.0 s < 12.0 s`).
3. Run the full focused set: `pytest tests/agent/test_memory_provider.py` — 77 passed (76 pre-existing + 1 new).

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regression test for this bug (`test_default_external_prefetch_timeout_keeps_slow_but_real_recalls`, vertical TDD: RED reproduced the drop symptom before the fix)
- [x] Existing tests still pass (77 passed vs measured baseline of 76 at `d3b25b52ad`; zero regressions)
- [x] Manual verification of the fix (deployed to a live instance: prefetch that previously skipped now completes)

## Risk Assessment

Low — the change widens one join window. Stuck-provider semantics are unchanged (a wedged call is still skipped and re-entered later; the provider thread is still a daemon thread). Worst case, a turn's prefetch merge waits up to 12 s instead of 8 s for a slow provider, and the bound still fails the provider fast and non-fatally. The new test's 9 s delay is a synthetic threshold probe between the old and new bounds, not a production latency.
title: fix(agent): raise external prefetch bound to 12s so real slow recalls are not dropped
